messages.author: 3b1202a93e4df335
messages.subject: Multiple isotopes
parts:
Hello, I am helping someone analyze their data which has been labeled with 3 types of isotope: light, medium, and heavy. We would like to run a linear mixed model with isotope as a random effect. Does MSstats support this type of analysis, or should we use lme4::lmer for now?

Thank you,
Brian Zhang

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: Multiple isotopes
parts: Does the labeling with three types of isotopes work like SILAC? If so, you can try MSstatsTMT (https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/MSstatsTMT.html) for the data analysis.

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: Multiple isotopes
parts: MSstats supports for the labeled-based SRM experiments (light and heavy peptides). And MSstatsTMT supports for iTRAQ and TMT experiments. You can use MSstatsTMT to analyze SILAC data but you may need to change the format of the data file to apply MSstatsTMT.  Can you show the first 10 rows of your psm file?
